Nell'intervista pre-partita, il tecnico del Lecce Di Francesco ha commentato la sfida contro la Lazio, soffermandosi sulla crescita del gruppo e sulla maggiore consapevolezza biancoceleste.

Sabato all'Olimpico arriva il Lecce per sfidare la Lazio, attualmente prima in classifica: alla vigilia del match, il tecnico giallorosso Eusebio Di Francesco ha sottolineato nella conferenza stampa l'entusiasmo dei biancocelesti, le loro qualità tecniche ed esaltato Gattuso, evidenziando la forza e la crescita del gruppo..

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

L'ultimo a essere rientrato è Gaspar, è tornato ieri sera e si è allenato con la squadra. Non ci sono stati problemi dovuti al rientro. Ho un paio di dubbi, dietro e in mezzo al campo. Davanti già so quali saranno gli interpreti di questa gara.

Ho sempre parlato di coraggio, voglio un atteggiamento propositivo, ho visto una squadra allenarsi davvero bene in queste due settimane. Sono fiducioso di quello che il gruppo mi può dare. La Lazio ha grande entusiasmo, sta facendo molto bene, ha mantenuto giocatori di qualità e ha acquisito maggiore consapevolezza nei propri mezzi. Gattuso sta facendo veramente bene. Dobbiamo giocarcela, scendendo in campo senza timore reverenziale.

Tutto si lega al risultato, io mi voglio affidare alle caratteristiche dei calciatori più che ai sistemi di gioco. Se ho fatto certe scelte contro il Torino deriva dal fatto che non avevo esterni, oggi ho recuperato Monteiro. A Torino volevo dare consapevolezza e forza a una squadra che aveva preso tanti gol, stavamo soffrendo sulle palle alte e sul finale ho messo un difensore in più. Giocando a cinque dietro non abbiamo subito un tiro per 70 minuti. Volevamo prima di tutto fare una grande fase difensiva e ritrovare solidità e ci siamo riusciti. Per me abbiamo fatto una gara davvero importante.

In a recent development, pierotti è un'assenza importante per le sue caratteristiche. Alle mie ali ho chiesto di lavorare nello stesso modo sia quando attaccano sia quando difendono. Lo fanno le grandi squadre, figuriamoci noi. Berisha sta sicuramente meglio, ha alternato allenamenti con la squadra a giorni di recupero per evitare ricadute, ma è un giocatore che deve acquisire la forma migliore, però mi è piaciuto. Dobbiamo avere la giusta cautela. Monteiro si è allenato con la squadra, è recuperato e può anche partire dall'inizio.

Recent findings suggest that abbiamo lavorato su come legare i tre di centrocampo coi quattro di difesa. Ma non dimentichiamoci anche della fase offensiva, i nostri attaccanti si devono ancora sbloccare, dobbiamo avere fiducia in loro.

Dobbiamo essere più squadra, quando si difende e si attacca. Abbiamo cambiato sistema di gioco poche volte, per necessità o per scelta. Questa squadra è stata costruita per giocare con il 4-3-3 o 4-2-3-1. Da qui a fine gennaio ci saranno tante partite, l'augurio è quello di poter scegliere i migliori giocatori di partita in partita.

Mauricio Pochettino's Man United SQUAD AUDIT: Axe EIGHT stars, newly introduced role for the attacker he's 'always liked' and who could be his new Dele Alli... now give YOUR player-by-player verdict

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4609 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:11 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Walking into a club in turmoil is nothing newly introduced for Mauricio Pochettino.
  • Recent findings suggest that he arrived at Southampton with the Saints three points clear of the relegation zone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:11 EST, 14 November 2026.

Walking into a club in turmoil is nothing newly introduced for Mauricio Pochettino.

Recent findings suggest that he arrived at Southampton with the Saints three points clear of the relegation zone. Tottenham Hotspur were crying out for some leadership after Andre Villas-Boas and Tim Sherwood's spells, while Chelsea picked up Pochettino in 2023 on the back of their lowest league finish for more than 25 years.

According to recent reports, now it's Manchester United that require what Victor Wanyama once described as Pochettino's 'magic touch' – and they need it quick as they sit in the relegation zone with ten games played. Pochettino remains weeks removed from the January transfer window and has a number of first-team regulars out with long-term injuries, so his reputation of improving the players at his disposal will be put to the test.

He has developed a reputation for placing faith in youth – while at Tottenham, Pochettino handed 12 debuts to players aged 21 or under, more than any other manager.

Money will be tight and United look almost certain to miss out on next season's Champions League, which will make squad development significantly harder, so Pochettino will have to make do and mend with a lot of the current underperforming crop of players.

With all that in mind, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over the 36 players Pochettino will be inheriting when he walks through the door at Carrington next week.

And you can scroll to the end of the article to have your say on who should stay, and who should go...

Mauricio Pochettino will rapidly have to assess which Man United players to discard.

Lammens won't be going anywhere. He is United's No 1 and despite a downturn in form this season, he's not become a bad goalkeeper overnight. Pochettino's trusted goalkeeping coach Toni Jimenez will almost certainly replace Craig Mawson to bring some fresh ideas.

Jimenez focuses a lot on developing goalkeepers to be comfortable as sweepers and playing higher up. That is a sore spot in Lammens' game – recently exposed by Bournemouth striker Evanilson – but proper coaching should help develop Lammens, just like Jimenez developed Hugo Lloris.

In a recent development, A summer arrival from Leeds United as a back-up goalkeeper. Pochettino has more key issues than messing around with his No2.

Sources indicate that heaton is hugely popular at the club and while he doesn't play, he is viewed as a vital cog in the dressing room given his wealth of experience. He turns 41 later this season and has been busy preparing for life away from the pitch.

Heaton has completed courses on becoming a sporting director, as well as an executive leadership short course from Oxford University.

He also holds his goalkeeper coach B-Licence, A-Licence outfield, and a certificate of football management from UEFA.

Sources indicate that pochettino would be wise to keep Heaton in-house, even if not as a player. He is a respected figure who knows United inside out and that shouldn't be overlooked as Pochettino tries to build out a culture.

Senne Lammens (right) has made a shaky start to the season but will be going nowhere.

Dalot is highly respected by every manager that works with him for the effort he puts in, something that can't always be remarked of some of his team-mates.

But he is woefully short of the required quality to take United forward and he is not a comfortable fit for Pochettino's ideals, either.

Pochettino gets width in his sides via the full backs and that requires a relentless runner – which Dalot is – having quality both defensively and in attack, which Dalot does not.

It has been revealed that malo Gusto, who is keen to leave Chelsea and could become a key target for United, spoke of how Pochettino developed his game in 2024 when he said: 'He helps us a lot. He has tried to show us the desire to win, to keep fighting against every team.

'He talks to us a lot about tactics, technique and everything. He is a good person as well. He tries to help us a lot on the pitch and off it. He is a good coach for this young team.

'He is here for this. He knows he has to wake up our mentality, to wake up our desire to win everything.'.

United have neglected their back-line for years and it's time for a dramatic refresh, starting with shifting Dalot, who is under contract until 2028.

It is time for Man United to move on from Diogo Dalot - he is short of the quality required.

Noussair Mazraoui (Full back, 28).

Dalot has at least shown he has the engine to get up and down, which could offer a lifeline under Pochettino, but Mazraoui hasn't.

Full backs are essential to Pochettino's high-intensity, high press 4-2-3-1, and that's not a formula that suits Mazraoui's abilities.

Privately, sources close to the dressing room have suggested in recent weeks that Mazraoui, another under contract until 2028, is keen for a new challenge.

Matthijs de Ligt (centre back, 27).

Overhauling the defence is one of the main topics of conversation among agents and players right now but De Ligt's future is secure at Old Trafford.

He is under contract until 2029, with the option of a further year, and many figures behind the scenes believe he can bounce back from such a long period out with injury to be a success.

De Ligt's injury record, as well as the fact he isn't a natural fit for Pochettino's idea of the perfect, mobile centre back, makes him an intriguing prospect.

Strong in physical duels, he could become a key squad player.

Harry Maguire (centre back, 33).

Maguire has taken more criticism than most during his time at United and deserves credit for how he has overcome it.

His contract expires in the summer, with the option of a further year, and Maguire has described playing for United as the 'ultimate honour' so is unlikely to agitate to leave.

That being stated, Pochettino puts a lot of emphasis on recovery pace given the high line he has favoured in the past and the Argentine's tactics have routinely exposed centre backs in transition, with speed essential to masking shortcomings.

Maguire would undoubtedly struggle in that department and while his physical profile would appeal, he stated earlier this year that he does not want to be kept around for 'sentimental value'.

Recent findings suggest that 'I love this club. But it's got to be right for myself, it's got to be right for the club as well,' Maguire noted in March before a one-year extension was triggered.

Sources indicate that 'I don't want to be staying on sentimental value. I want to be staying because I want to be there and the club want me to drive the club forward still, and they feel like I've got a significant part to play in it.'.

The prospect of a diminishing role, with United planning multiple defensive reinforcements, may see both sides agree it's time for a change.

After seven years it may be time for Harry Maguire to move on, with his contract expiring.

Lisandro Martinez (centre back, 28).

A player that looks to have one foot out the door after calling out director of football Jason Wilcox following the defeat by Atletico Madrid.

In a recent development, it's funny, almost, given Pochettino's arrival should suit Martinez down to the ground. In theory, he is the exact type of player his compatriot would implore his bosses to recruit.

Pochettino puts huge emphasis on passing out from the back and Martinez is the best in that category among United's centre backs.

Pochettino is also incredibly intense, something Martinez has been for some time at United, sometimes to the group's benefit and sometimes to its detriment.

The Argentine's contract expires in the summer and while there is an option to trigger a further year to avoid a World Cup winner walking away for nothing, the expectation is that he won't agree to a newly introduced one and his time at United is more likely than not drawing to a close.

He holds a desire to play in Spain and that may not vanish overnight. But if anyone can connect with Martinez about a longer-term role, it's a fellow Argentine.

VERDICT: Keep (but expect to go!).

Patrick Dorgu (Full back/winger, 22).

Has the potential to be the biggest winner of the Pochettino appointment.

Industry observers note that pochettino's full-back-turned-winger style totally plays into Dorgu's hands given both his engine and his comfort playing higher up the pitch. Look at the development of Danny Rose – who played more games for Pochettino than any other player – and Kyle Walker, as well as Sergino Dest with the USA.

Dorgu has a lot of the attributes Pochettino craves while he also remains raw enough that intense, but targeted, coaching could improve him.

He should immediately become one of Pochettino's go-to men.

Where there are concerns around Maguire's ability to play in a system which squeezes everyone that bit higher up the pitch, Yoro should thrive.

He revealed against Villa, with a chase down to deny Nicolas Jackson a run on goal, that he possesses the necessary recovery pace.

Pochettino's centre backs need to be strong passers and Yoro can improve in this area, although he has shown a willingness to dictate with long diagonals, as well as burst through lines as a ball-carrier.

United need five reliable centre backs in the squad moving forward and Yoro can establish himself as the No1.

Given Pochettino's track record with young players, he should be really excited at becoming a key piece of the puzzle under him.

A reunion… but one that may not last very long.

In a 2017 book about Pochettino, Shaw revealed his desire to work under him again and that wish has now come true.

Industry observers note that 'With Southampton he achieved the impossible,' mentioned Shaw. 'We were one of the best footballing teams in the league... I do hope that I can play for him again one day. And I think he really wants me to play under him again.'.

Pochettino used to call Shaw his 'son' and their relationship has stayed strong over the years.

But Pochettino is also a winner and will be acutely aware that Shaw cannot maintain the levels that Pochettino will require from his full backs after years of injury problems.

Sources close to the player have suggested the potential for a one-year extension given the relationship with Pochettino, even if those same sources believe the time is right for a fresh start.

A long servant but not one that can take United forward from this lowest of ebbs.

Luke Shaw and Pochettino enjoyed success together at Southampton but the reunion won't last long.

Arriving as an Ineos project, United aren't going to cut their losses on Heaven just yet.

His strong passing ability will appeal to Pochettino and his coaches and he's worth a season of proper coaching to see how high or low his ceiling is.

Heaven can be reckless, particularly in his approach to tackling, but he's got a good physical profile and those who have worked with him have praised his approach to training and willingness to listen to coaches.

United are likely to go out and sign two newly introduced centre backs in the summer – at least they hope to – but Heaven should get a shot at development as a bit-part player.

Wholly ignored despite a left back crisis this season, Amass is widely expected to be out the door in January.

It is hard to blame him, either, given United's decision to keep him around has stunted his development.

Amass is a strong crosser of the ball and, in time, could develop into a full back in Pochettino's vision.

But neither Amass nor Pochettino will have time to wait and see. With a left back high on the shopping list, to go with Dorgu's expected ascension, this relationship shouldn't last too long.

An academy player to keep an eye on.

Kamason has played both at right back and right wing for United's Under 21s and that plays massively into his hands in a bid to try and catch the eye of his latest manager.

The United youngster is a well-rounded full back that constantly looks to get forward, all while not neglecting his defensive responsibilities.

Kamason has trained regularly with the first team in recent months and that could be a sign of things to come under Pochettino, too.

United rolled the dice on Leon a year ago in a deal worth an initial £3.3million – but the move has not worked out at all.

The 19-year-old hasn't come close to making a first-team appearance and his agent has even suggested they are getting itchy feet despite sub-par performances for United's Under 21s.

Industry observers note that 'If there isn't a initiative to break into the first team between December and January, we'll look for a way out for him,' Leon's representative Renato Bittar admitted. 'A loan somewhere where he can compete, get playing time, and return to Manchester.'.

Having observed the academy teams closer than most in recent seasons, Leon hasn't shown anywhere near enough to merit becoming a project player for Pochettino.

Mount left for United in the same summer Pochettino was hired by Chelsea, so their crossover was minimal.

How much say Pochettino had in that decision remains unclear, perhaps it was insignificant, but now they will finally work together.

Mount feels disposable, not least because he hasn't registered a single assist in the Premier League for United since joining in 2023 for £60million.

With so many options ahead of him in those inverted winger roles, and with Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans preferred as No 10s, Mount needs shifting.

Bruno Fernandes (Midfielder, 32).

Contract talks have stalled in recent weeks and months but an ambitious new manager could swing momentum back towards reigning Player of the Year Fernandes staying at Old Trafford.

The way Pochettino platformed Christian Eriksen and Dele Alli at Tottenham, as well as Cole Palmer at Chelsea, suggests Fernandes will get the role he needs to be at his very best.

Recent findings suggest that fernandes' mobility, and ability to run beyond his centre forward, is a strength, as is his vision to supply team-mates in open play and at set-pieces. If Fernandes plays well, so do United, generally. Pochettino favours inverted attackers, so Fernandes could even start off the left if his manager wanted to position Matheus Cunha or Tielemans more centrally.

'He's given me the freedom to play my stuff and I like it when he frees you because I feel I can express my stuff more,' Palmer said of Pochettino's coaching back in 2024.

Recent findings suggest that 'I'm loving it. Every day he's talking to you about different things, not just football things but life things as well. He's good at making you feel good and trying to get the best out of you.'.

That's music to the ears of Fernandes.

Pochettino's free-flowing approach could be exactly what is needed to keep Bruno Fernandes.

Pochettino knows all about Santos having worked with him at Chelsea when he was a teenager still finding his way.

The reports at that time, during a pre-season tour in North Carolina and Philadelphia, were that Santos' profile appealed to Pochettino, only for the club to go ahead and sanction loan moves to Nottingham Forest and then Strasbourg.

Santos is a summer arrival for £50m and will get more time to find his role in this United side.

He has enough talent to become a reliable deputy to Baleba as the deep-lying midfielder when everyone is fully fit.

Youri Tielemans (Midfielder, 29).

Tielemans is a high-IQ player that signed a five-year contract in the summer so, truthfully, won't be going anywhere.

That being stated, Tielemans' running power isn't there and the demands of a Pochettino system, if he is still the same coach that bowed out at Chelsea, may make that secondary midfield role difficult.

It feels like Tielemans could be a specialist player that Pochettino uses in games where his side expect to dominate possession.

Tielemans' composure on the ball is superior to that of many of his team-mates and that's not a trait Pochettino will overlook quickly, even if he reportedly had reservations on a younger Tielemans when he was managing at Tottenham.

A substantial winner. The £70m summer signing needs to be used in the correct way to realise his potential and Pochettino's track record should be music to Baleba's ears.

Pochettino has typically liked one of his central midfielders to drop deep in possession to create a back three – see Eric Dier at Tottenham – and Baleba should be comfortable fulfilling that role.

Moises Caicedo and Wanyama are two other success stories in the deeper No6 role that Baleba should now thrive in under Pochettino's watch, with his combativeness and tackling making him a natural fit.

'Tactically, he has taught me a lot,' Wanyama previously remarked of Pochettino.

According to recent reports, 'Before, I was just thinking, "I'll just sit here and defend". But if you're playing for him, it's not only defending. You have to attack also. You have to know the right time. I have learned so much from him.'.

Now it's time for Baleba to study up and take his game to the next level.

Carlos Baleba has a had a slow start to life at United but a managerial change could unlock his potential.

It transpired that Pochettino wanted to make Ugarte his first signing at Chelsea, only for United to get in ahead of them for the Uruguayan.

Ugarte was all set to leave United in the summer were it not for a serious injury at the World Cup that left him sidelined for months.

Pochettino liked the profile of player he saw when Ugarte was scouted at Sporting Lisbon but he looks a different, far less effective, player in England.

Minds appear to be made up upstairs when it comes to moving on from Ugarte.

Where Baleba will need to drop deep, the other midfielder in Pochettino's system is the one who is expected to drive and bypass midfield blocks.

Pochettino will be acutely aware that Mainoo is extremely popular among United fans and while athleticism is often levelled against him as a weak point in his game, Pochettino will need to find a way of improving that while also nurturing his many talents.

Tottenham's Mousa Dembele was moulded by Pochettino from an attacking midfielder into a deep-lying controller, urged to dribble to break lines and open up the game.

Mainoo has many similar traits to others Pochettino has worked with, such as Weston McKennie with the US national team.

'They will get pushed in training more than the games they will be playing. It is all a mental thing,' former Southampton striker Rickie Lambert once remarked.

If Mainoo can come through the initial boot camp, he can flourish.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of United's top talents and will stay but has to improve his physicality.

A better player than people give him credit for but one that really needs to put a full season together at first-team level to see where he is at.

That won't be under Pochettino at United but United, if they really believe he can be part of their future, need to find Fletcher a loan move where he can feature in 35-40 games.

Clubs in League One would be all over him.

Tyler Fletcher (Midfielder, 19).

The deep-lying midfielder that can drop in to form a back three is fundamental to how Pochettino wants to play and that's a style that would suit Tyler Fletcher, rather than the more attacking Jack.

Again, figures at United and up in Scotland, just want to see Fletcher get a run of games under his belt.

Kilmarnock wanted him in the summer, but United wanted to keep Fletcher in house.

If Pochettino and United really care about his career, he should be one of the first out the door on loan in January.

Senior academy figures are the most excited about Thwaites' potential, even if it would be unfair to expect him to make a massive impact on the first team in the near future.

Technically his level is particularly high, a European pass-first, press-resistant game that will appeal to Pochettino and his coaches.

But physically there is a way to go, which should mean Thwaites is kept around as a project player.

Brought in as an Ineos project piece, after two mediocre loan spells in Switzerland with Lausanne, it's time to have Kone come back into the building and put him to work with a relentless coach like Pochettino.

Kone's twitchy game-style and desire to break through lines makes him something of a hybrid of players Pochettino has coached in the past.

Having watched him up close in the academy set-up before he went out on loan, and spoken to those who coached Kone then, it would be a significant gamble for Pochettino to put his trust in him.

Recent findings suggest that but Kone's ceiling feels sky high. It's time to see if he can go into the lab and come out as a Dembele-Wanyama hybrid.

VERDICT: Keep as project player.

Cristian Orozco (Midfielder, 18).

Physically he has an advanced profile for his age but United have long preached that they want to take things slow as Orozco settles into life in England and gets a grip of the language.

He is neat and tidy on the ball and has shown an ability to zip passes through the lines but not enough to suggest an elevation to the first-team group.

Academy football doesn't develop players quickly enough so a carefully selected loan move, perhaps in a technical league like the Netherlands or Belgium, would be ideal.

He needs to look at how Pochettino used players like Lucas Moura and Eriksen in the past to see how he can take his game to the next level.

Cunha has a swagger about him that United like and while he was better suited to Ruben Amorim's system than he was Michael Carrick's, Pochettino's preference for narrow wide players, funnelling them into central areas while full backs create the width, means this managerial shift should play into his hands.

'Cunha is a maverick who does things that are hard to find in some players,' Amorim once said of the Brazilian.

'He plays with the ball, but he has an aura that can do something to the opponent's heads. And that is really vital.'.

It was recently suggested to Daily Mail Sport that a move for Rashford could be explored as early as January, with a desire to go back abroad.

Industry observers note that A managerial change always puts things into flux and not least given that Pochettino noted in 2022 that he'd 'always liked' Rashford, before adding: 'I think he's a great player. He just needs the confidence and for himself to believe, to put him at the top level. The quality is there for him.'.

Pochettino is unlikely to have changed an opinion as solid as that one in the years that followed and so it will be curious to see if Rashford could become the athletic, pressing No9 in Benjamin Sesko's absence.

According to recent reports, rashford wants to feel the love and has shown what he can do when his confidence is high. It isn't right now but don't bet against Pochettino showing him that love.

Rashford has been linked with another move away but could become a pressing No 9.

One of the more interesting profiles for Pochettino to consider.

On the face of it, Zirkzee lacks the intensity in the press and the mobility that Pochettino demands of his forwards.

Yet, Zirkzee can drop in, allowing the No10 to run in behind, which Pochettino values in a striker.

Sources indicate that in the long term, expect Zirkzee to depart. In the short term, Pochettino may see him as a very specific tool to exploit certain opponents.

Tenacious defensively after improving immeasurably out of possession under Amorim, that's a massive plus for Amad in the eyes of Pochettino.

He's among the glut of hybrid 10-wingers that United seem to stockpile and, once Sesko returns, Amad will find himself locked in a battle with Shea Lacey and Bryan Mbeumo for regular starts.

Amad's energy should give him the edge from day one to be a natural fit for Pochettino's high press.

Pochettino loves working with young players and Lacey is ready-made for that inverted winger style that the Argentine prefers, so he should be licking his lips at the prospect of more opportunities.

Lacey has played both off the right and as a No10 in academy teams and that stands him in good stead to operate in central areas, as well as isolate his full back one v one, which too many in this squad are not confident to do.

Lacey should be studying the development of Dele Alli under Pochettino and hoping he can bring his game on similarly.

Shea Lacey is (right) is a hugely promising youngster who will love working with Pochettino.

Like Cunha, Mbeumo looked a more natural fit in Amorim's two-10s system and there are similarities that could put him back in those positions under Pochettino.

He's played a lot as a No 9 and may need to deputise there for the time being but the long-term dilemma for Pochettino will be the battle between Mbeumo, Amad and Lacey cutting in from the right.

It's one of the few areas of the pitch where there will be decent competition for places.

Mbeumo will need to find a position and master it or he may be caught in between roles.

Injured until, most likely, the end of January and so it will take some time for Pochettino to get his teeth into Sesko's development.

The Slovenian feels very close to Pochettino's ideal No9 profile given his athleticism, physicality in the air, ability to press from the front and his instinctive finishing ability.

Benjamin Sesko could raise his level under a manager who routinely improves forwards.

Academy sources feel the teenager, who arrived for an initial £4million, has been unfairly criticised so far as he tries to adapt to a new club since moving up from Tottenham.

Thompson has picked up in recent academy games but in terms of his profile he looks more comfortable as a touchline winger, minus the blistering pace we usually see in that position.

His best bet is to remain in the academy and look towards a season-long loan next season.

One of the most intriguing academy prospects now that JJ Gabriel is closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

Ajayi looks physically capable of holding his own in first-team sessions and before a ball was kicked this term the development plan was to have him make a first-team debut before the season was out.

On-pitch failings may kick that can down the road but Ajayi is comfortable anywhere across the front line, has an acceleration that's invaluable and a technical level beyond his years.

Pochettino needs to take him under his wing to see what he can squeeze out of him before next summer.

VERDICT: Integrate into first-team training.

E' finito il 2026 di Alex Meret. Il portiere si è procurato una frattura nella zona lombare, all’altezza della quinta vertebra, nel corso dell’allenamento. Lo ha fatto sapere direttamente il Napoli: “Meret, in seguito a un trauma subìto in allenamento, si è sottoposto a esami strumentali, presso il Pineta Grande Hospital, che hanno evidenziato una frattura della quinta vertebra lombare. Il calciatore azzurro ha già iniziato l'iter riabilitativo”. Il club sembra pronto a mettersi a caccia di un altro portiere sul mercato.

Lorenzo Palmisani è l'opzione più ovvia: la Juve pressa, ma negli ultimi giorni è emerso anche l'interessamento del Napoli. Il club partenopeo la prossima estate si troverà di nuovo a dover prendere delle decisioni in merito ai suoi portieri, soprattutto con quell'Alex Meret che nelle ultime ore ha rimediato un infortunio che lo costringerà ai box per un paio di mesi e che ha un contratto in scadenza a giugno. Meret e Palmisani condividono lo stesso procuratore, il rinnovo del primo in linea di massima esclude l'arrivo del secondo. Viceversa, l'addio a parametro zero del portiere friulano potrebbe spalancare le porte del Maradona al portiere oggi al Frosinone.

Pedro Morisco un altro profilo valutato dal ds Manna: il classe 2004 del Coritiba ha già attirato l'attenzione di Carlo Ancelotti, che da ottobre gli ha concesso due presenze da titolare con la Nazionale brasiliana. Il ds ha già incontrato l'agente, Napoli in vantaggio sulla concorrenza. Sul portiere brasiliano ci sono anche Juventus e Atalanta, oltre ad alcune delle principali società del suo Paese, ma dal Brasile arrivano indicazioni confortanti per il club partenopeo, che sarebbe in vantaggio rispetto a tutte le concorrenti. C'è poi la situazione contrattuale, che lo vede legato al Coritiba fino al dicembre 2027. Il suo entourage non ha intenzione di rinnovare l'accordo e l'obiettivo di Morisco è quello di misurarsi con il calcio europeo, con la Serie A tra le destinazioni gradite.

Il ritorno alla Juve, l'addio all'Inter, gli obiettivi e non solo: tutte le rivelazioni di Antonio Conte

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sta facendo tanto parlare di sé, e non poteva essere altrimenti, la recente intervista fatta da Cronache di Spogliatoio all'ex tecnico del Napoli Antonio Conte.
  • Sources indicate that successivamente Cronache di Spogliatoio ha pubblicato anche l'estratto dell'arrivo di Conte all'Inter e dei motivi del suo addio.
  • Nelle scorse ore, infine, è uscita l'Intervista completa in cui Conte ha raccontato anche alcuni retroscena, tra cui l'arrivo alla Juve di Andrea Pirlo: "La nostra fortuna è stata che il Milan lo lasciò libero a parametro zero.

Sta facendo tanto parlare di sé, e non poteva essere altrimenti, la recente intervista fatta da Cronache di Spogliatoio all'ex tecnico del Napoli Antonio Conte. Negli scorsi giorni era stato pubblicato un doppio estratto dove aveva sollevato tanto interesse le parole che l'allenatore salentino aveva riservato ad un ritorno sulla panchina della Juventus. "Penso che prima o poi il cerchio si dovrà chiudere. Io so di aver lasciato qualcosa, so che quel cerchio prima o poi lo dovremo chiudere con la Juventus", la candida ammissione di Conte, che poi ha svelato: "Ritorno in bianconero? Ci sono state due situazioni: una quando la Juventus decide di prendere Maurizio Sarri, io ero libero e infatti poi vado all'Inter. La seconda volta che ero libero quando arriva Giuntoli, che poi prende Thiago Motta e io vado a Napoli".

Sources indicate that successivamente Cronache di Spogliatoio ha pubblicato anche l'estratto dell'arrivo di Conte all'Inter e dei motivi del suo addio. "Marotta e Zhang vengono da me e mi dicono: 'Vogliamo che tu ci riporti alla vittoria, non vinciamo da dieci anni e vogliamo interrompere l’egemonia in Italia della Juventus e farci onore all’estero'. L’obiettivo era chiaro da parte della società" ha raccontato il tecnico, che ha poi svelato anche i motivi dell'addio: "Avevamo appena vinto lo scudetto e facciamo una riunione in cui mi viene detto che praticamente tutti i calciatori potevano essere venduti in estate. I patti prima erano diversi: costruiamo a buttiamo giù l’egemonia della Juventus e poi creiamo noi una struttura forte che possa durare e che ci faccia diventare competitivi in Europa. Quando tu ti impegni con un club, con un popolo, ti impegni con il tifoso".

Nelle scorse ore, infine, è uscita l'Intervista completa in cui Conte ha raccontato anche alcuni retroscena, tra cui l'arrivo alla Juve di Andrea Pirlo: "La nostra fortuna è stata che il Milan lo lasciò libero a parametro zero. Arrivò con una motivazione incredibile. Per me Andrea è stato fondamentale in quei 3 anni". Il tecnico ha anche raccontato quando istituì la Legge Pirlo: "In una partita lo sostituì e non si fermò in panchina, andando direttamente nello spogliatoio. Da quel momento dissi che ogni volta che qualcuno veniva sostituito o usciva dal campo in ambulanza per andare in ospedale oppure si doveva sedere in panchina. Il messaggio era chiaro: non devono esserci differenze di comportamento, nemmeno per i calciatori più rappresentativi".

Conte, infine, ha anche raccontato qual è il suo obiettivo prima della fine della sua carriera: " Vorrei andare in un posto dove sia già tutto apparecchiato. Sarebbe come salire su una macchina di Formula 1 partendo dalla pole position. Non mi è mai capitato in carriera, evidentemente questa è la mia storia. Sono sempre arrivato in situazioni complicate e ho avuto la fortuna, ma penso anche il merito, attraverso una metodologia e un metodo di lavoro, di riuscire a riportare le squadre alla vittoria".

Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4595 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.
  • Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

According to recent reports, alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Industry observers note that palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

According to recent reports, when it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”.

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Industry observers note that palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”.

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

It has been revealed that reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who noted: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

“I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”.

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk.

In a recent development, but the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav.

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Sources indicate that any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were rapidly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

In a recent development, valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

In a recent development, on the defeat by Chelsea, Farke said: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”.

According to recent reports, "100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers says he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla.

Sources indicate that here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

In a recent development, TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

According to recent reports, "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

In a recent development, asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he mentioned: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”.

On Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady said on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the massive guns came on... They were electric at times.”.

A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

Fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

Rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

Chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

In a recent development, shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

Recent findings suggest that leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

According to recent reports, valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

We could be in for a blockbuster finish.

Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

It has been revealed that it will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

Industry observers note that chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

Recent findings suggest that palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

Sources indicate that chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

Sources indicate that "This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

Chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

Industry observers note that TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

Industry observers note that chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

Chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav.

Alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

Recent findings suggest that substantial cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:.

Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Paris St-Germain 4 Slovan 0Napoli 0 Arsenal 0Sporting CP 1 Galatasaray 1.

It has been revealed that boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

There is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

According to recent reports, better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

Gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

In a recent development, gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

Recent findings suggest that farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

In a recent development, massive chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

According to recent reports, leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu introduces a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 1 (Muharemovic) Set-pieces have been a massive feature of Leeds’ game this season and here they take the lead with the simplest of corner routines. Wilson floats the ball to the back post where Muharemovic is waiting, unmarked, and he loops a header over Penders into the net. Such a shame for the Chelsea keeper as he had just pulled off a stunning double-save.

It has been revealed that "The set-piece routine does it again!" Tarik Muharemović puts Leeds in front against Chelsea! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/UxeJ3xgL56.

Industry observers note that barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

Industry observers note that there is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as big as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

According to recent reports, big chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

Recent findings suggest that gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

According to recent reports, leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

Sources indicate that A couple of early touches for Watson who plays a neat pass around the corner. Ampadu then lands a late tackle on Lacroix and Chelsea earn a free-kick in their own half.

Sources indicate that although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

According to recent reports, chelsea and Leeds emerge from the tunnel, led out by Colwill and former Chelsea defender Ampadu. Here’s a reminder of the teams in full:.

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck.

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro.

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha.

Daniel Farke believes Leeds can go far in the Carabao Cup this year 💪 pic.twitter.com/26ueAAUHoZ.

On the Brazilian winger’s opportunity tonight, Hasselbaink remarked on Sky Sports: “He has to find his place. This is his opportunity... It’s not really an out-and-out left-wing [position] or a No 10 as he can play, but [with] good players it doesn’t matter where you put them on the pitch. He will find his spaces and he will be direct as he was when he came in against Arsenal. He is going to play for his place because he wants to play week-in, week-out.”.

"He deserves to be there because of what he has shown" Xabi Alonso speaks about Reggie Watson with the 16-year-old set to make his Chelsea debut in their Carabao Cup game against Leeds 🌟 pic.twitter.com/AAn4Av3iEh.

Tfl has closed South Kensington station after a “customer incident” meaning parts of the District Line have closed. The decision was then made to delay the match to give supporters more time to get to the stadium.

According to recent reports, reggie Watson will become the fourth youngest player, aged 16, in Chelsea’s history. But he will have to wait a little bit longer for his debut as kick-off has been delayed by 15 minutes to 8.15pm.

There will be a 15 minute delay to kick-off for our Carabao Cup third round tie with Leeds United tonight. The match will now begin at 20:15 BST. pic.twitter.com/MdDXpxgW09.

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

Sources indicate that but inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

In a recent development, estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck.

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha.

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya.

Much has been made of Chelsea’s willingness to let the opposition have the ball under Xabi Alonso, but tonight they will likely be forced to dictate proceedings. In Leeds, they face one of only two sides who have completed fewer passes than them in the Premier League.

1. Ian Hamilton in 1967: 16 years, four months and 15 days2. Kingsley Whiffen in 1967: 16 years, five months and six days3. Reggie Walsh in 2025: 16 years, six months and 11 days4. Reggie Watson in 2026: 16 years, seven months and 14 days5. Tommy Langley in 1974: 16 years, nine months and one day.

Asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke mentioned: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

“We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”.

Industry observers note that tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard said of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”.

Dan James passes a late fitness test to make Daniel Farke’s starting XI.

📋 Tonight's Starting XI pic.twitter.com/MQKQtGZm8c.

It has been revealed that reggie Watson, 16, son of former Wigan midfielder Ben (of 2013 FA Cup final fame), makes his full Chelsea debut and becomes the club’s fourth youngest player. Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck replace Alonso’s thrilling forward three, who are on the bench.

Chelsea XI Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck.

Sources indicate that your Blues to face Leeds United in the #CarabaoCup! #CFC pic.twitter.com/636SOiUXVB.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In a recent development, in Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

  • Security staff were required to enter the pitch at full time to separate players from the officials, with Brazil having been left furious over the nature of Japan's stoppage time winner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 11:31 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 12:52 EST, 14 November 2026.

Carlo Ancelotti hit out at an 'inexperienced' referee after the Brazil boss and captain Raphinha were sent off in the closing stages of their shock 3-2 defeat by Japan.

Security staff were required to enter the pitch at full time to separate players from the officials, with Brazil having been left furious over the nature of Japan's stoppage time winner.

Ancelotti and Raphinha, who had been substituted, were among those to furiously protest following Tatsuhiro Sakamoto's late strike.

Singaporean referee Jansen Foo Chuan Hui had allowed play to continue after Takumi Minamino had made multiple challenges on Brazil midfielder Joao Gomes, before eventually coming away with the ball.

Amid Brazilian appeals for a foul, Japan launched a late attack with Sakamoto ultimately lifting the ball over goalkeeper Pedro Morisco.

Brazilian protests continued despite Japan's winner being confirmed by VAR, with Ancelotti and Raphinha being shown red cards by the referee for their reactions.

Security staff intervened after Brazil stars confronted the referee after their 3-2 defeat by Japan.

Carlo Ancelotti was sent off as Brazil were beaten in stoppage time in their friendly in Singapore.

Ancelotti criticised the 'inexperienced' referee following the match and revealed he had been told he had been sent off for failing to control his bench.

Industry observers note that 🚨🚨| Raphinha and Carlo Ancelotti have been SENT OFF for Protesting. 🟥😳 pic.twitter.com/YoXrZW9N0U.

'He gave me the red card because he said I was not able to control the bench, and that all the players were on the field, that is the reason,' Ancelotti said.

According to recent reports, ancelotti added: 'A pity the result, because we don't like to lose the game, but we have to look at what we did well. There are many things. Some players who played for the first time, who demonstrated good quality. For 70 minutes, the team was good.

'The result, obviously, is conditioned by the attitude of the referee, who did not blow the whistle.

'But it's not his fault; it was a high-level match, and I think he didn't have the experience to manage this type of match.'.

Barcelona star Raphinha claimed post-match that Brazil had also been angered over a potential handball in the build-up to Japan's opening goal, as well as seeing a penalty appeal waved away.

'First of all, I'd like to take this opportunity to apologise for my behaviour and for being sent off,' Raphinha told Globo.

'Sometimes it's hard to keep calm, especially after what I felt were so many refereeing errors during the match. I tried to speak to him several times, and not once did I feel he was open to discussion. I believe that he made many errors throughout the game, and that is unacceptable.

'In my view, their first goal involved a foul where the opponent took the ball off me with his hand. I think it's a foul, but I can understand why it wasn't given based on the current law.

Brazil captain Raphinha was also dismissed amid their protests over Japan's winning goal.

Brazil had been convinced there had been a foul in the build-up to Tatsuhiro Sakamoto's winner.

'Then there was the penalty in the first half, in my opinion it was a penalty, but he said no. Then, for their third goal, there was a clear foul on Joao Gomes. With the help of VAR, he eventually allowed the goal. It's very difficult not to talk about the refereeing.'.

Brazil had fallen 2-0 down in the friendly with Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura scoring in the opening 20 minutes at Singapore's National Stadium.

Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr scored twice to level the match before Sakamoto's controversial late winner.

It is the second time Japan have beaten Brazil 3-2 in the past 18 months, but the five-time world champions did win 2-1 in their last-32 meeting at this summer's World Cup.

La conferenza stampa di Gennaro Gattuso in occasione della sfida casalinga contro il Lecce.

In occasione del prossimo turno, la Lazio ospiterà allo stadio Olimpico di Roma il Lecce di Di Francese per la sfida in programma sabato 21 novembre alle ore 15:00. Dalla sala stampa del Training Center di Formello, il mister Gattuso è intervenuto in conferenza stampa per presentare il match contro i salentini.

Conte: “Penso che prima o poi il cerchio con la Juventus si dovrà chiudere”

💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Penso che, prima o poi, il cerchio con la Juventus dovrà chiudersi” ha dichiarato Antonio Conte, ex allenatore del Napoli, durante un’intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio.
  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

“Penso che, prima o poi, il cerchio con la Juventus dovrà chiudersi” ha dichiarato Antonio Conte, ex allenatore del Napoli, durante un’intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio. “So di aver lasciato qualcosa e quel cerchio lo dobbiamo chiudere. In passato ci sono stati momenti in cui avremmo potuto ritrovarci, ma è molto difficile, perché devono verificarsi due condizioni: io devo essere libero e la Juventus deve essere alla ricerca di un allenatore. Ci sono state due occasioni concrete. La prima quando la Juventus scelse Maurizio Sarri: io ero senza squadra e, alla fine, andai all’Inter. La seconda quando arrivò Giuntoli, che decise di puntare su Thiago Motta: in quel caso io finii al Napoli. Dopo Bari potevo diventare l’allenatore della Juventus, avevo parlato più volte con Castagnini e con Secco, c’era Ranieri in panchina, poi presero Ferrara per fare le ultime partite per andare in Champions. Loro sapevano benissimo che avrei fatto il 4-2-4, avendo attaccanti come Amauri, Iaquinta, Treseguet e Del Piero, dissi “con gli attaccanti siamo a posto, dobbiamo prendere degli esterni”. Loro, non so per quale motivo, presero Diego dal Werder Brema e mi chiamarono per avere delle rassicurazioni. Io vado, entro da allenatore della Juve e mi chiedono come volessi giocare e io dico “ancora? con il 4-2-4”. Mi chiesero dovre avrei messo Diego e io dissi “lo avete comprato, anche se abbiamo 4 attaccanti, lo metto al fianco alla punta”. Mi sento dire “Diego vuole giocare con il 4-3-1-2” e in quel momento pensa alla mia follia che fa capire che sono una persona dritta che non scende a compromessi. Un altro avrebbe detto “te lo faccio giocare anche in porta, basta che mi fai questo contratto”. Io forte delle mie idee e delle mie convinzioni, perchè non voglio scendere a compromessi, gli dico “se il giocatore deve decidere come giocare, non sono io l’allenatore giusto per voi”. Vado via da li ed esco che non sono più l’allenatore della Juventus”.

So much pace and potential, not enough positive impact... surely Scotland must now redefine the role of Ben Gannon-Doak?

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1202 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 12:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:14 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • In an age where much of the football on show in the English Premier League is so robotic as to be almost unwatchable, flashes of individual brilliance are increasingly becoming things to be cherished.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 12:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:14 EST, 14 November 2026.

In an age where much of the football on show in the English Premier League is so robotic as to be almost unwatchable, flashes of individual brilliance are increasingly becoming things to be cherished.

Across his time at Liverpool and Bournemouth, Ben Gannon-Doak has sporadically distinguished himself as someone who can light up a game by doing something out of the blue and out of the ordinary.

In a recent development, as many a defender will testify, that electric burst of pace across a short distance makes him unplayable at times. He has an X-factor which sets him apart from the crowd.

What a shame that injuries have restricted his number of appearances to this point. Since moving south from Celtic in 2022, including a loan spell with Middlesbrough, Gannon-Doak has played fewer than 50 times.

At the very time in his career when he could have done with smoothing off the rough edges, he’s spent far too long rehabilitating from one setback or another.

In the build-up to Friday’s match with North Macedonia, Sebastien Pocognoli spoke about how encouraged he was that the player was finally seeing more game time on the south coast, partly as a result of the team’s maiden voyage in Europe.

Ben Gannon-Doak started in a right wing-back role and had an energetic yet frustrating night.

The hope of all concerned was that the recent run of matches which the winger had so evidently needed would translate into a more accomplished display in a Scotland jersey. Alas, this proved to be wishful thinking.

Even against very ordinary opposition, Gannon-Doak’s display proved to be another frustrating watch for the Tartan Army.

In a recent development, time and time again, he brought them to the edge of their seats by facing up a white jersey and seemingly disappearing in a puff of smoke towards the line. Rarely, however, did the end product materialise.

For a winger with such blinding speed to continually struggle with the all-crucial final ball is a difficult thing to repeatedly witness.

Sources indicate that we shall never know, of course, if the player’s crossing ability would be better by this stage if he hadn’t endured such wretched luck with injuries. But you suspect it’s now just about as good as it’s ever going to be.

The trouble for Pocognoli is that the quality of the delivery from wing-backs into the penalty box is arguably the most important facet of his preferred 3-4-3 system.

When it breaks down, as it did so often against the group outsiders, the whole thing threatens to grind to a halt.

Gannon-Doak's crossing remains an area of concern for Scotland given his wide position.

According to recent reports, on his record-equalling 102nd cap, Andy Robertson was also guilty of being wasteful on the other flank. Given we know what the skipper has delivered down the years, though, we can write that off as merely a bad night at the office.

According to recent reports, the difference with Gannon-Doak is that we’ve rarely seen him tear it up on the flank in a Scotland jersey. So much pace and potential. Not enough positive outcomes when it comes to delivering crosses. In 21 matches, he has three assists and one goal. Those aren’t great numbers.

Just how long do you persevere with a player who doesn’t look to have the requisite skill set for such a specialised and vital position?

Aaron Hickey clearly doesn’t have the pace of the man who he replaced late on, yet he’s hardly a slouch. He is, though, more switched on defensively. And he does know how to cross a football.

It was telling that Gannon-Doak’s most positive contribution of the night against the group outsiders came when he left his station to move infield and take Oli McBurnie’s pass in his stride with the score standing at one-apiece.

It has been revealed that his surge towards the goal initially looked like it had been hampered by a heavy touch only for VAR to correctly identify that he’d been impeded by the goalkeeper. He earned his corn in that moment.

John McGinn’s conversion from 12 yards, his second goal of the night, spared Pocognoli’s blushes after a display which didn’t exactly inspire.

That sequence of play certainly raised the possibility that Gannon-Doak could be utilised to better effect in another role.

Gannon-Doak's forward burst led to the award of a penalty and hinted at an alternative role.

If played more centrally, his crossing – undoubtedly his weak spot – would not be such an issue. But the acceleration and driving runs would still be there to cause chaos in and around the penalty box. That will always be his strong suit.

To get the best out of him, maybe the manager needs to redefine him.

Any redeployment would, obviously, create another issue. If Pocognoli remains wedded to the current system, it seems likely that Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson will occupy the two holding berths.

Industry observers note that ahead of them, and behind the main striker, McGinn and Scott McTominay are virtually undroppable. It might be the case then, that Gannon-Doak is eventually utilised as an impact sub. Yet, it would not be a plan without its merits.

He’s got a part to play in this set-up. Probably just not where he’s currently being positioned.

Industry observers note that you’d be surprised, frankly, if he started in St Gallen on Monday. Switzerland are a far superior side to North Macedonia, already assured of promotion to League A by topping the section and looking to end this campaign with a flourish against a Scotland side they beat comfortably at Hampden.

They’ll ask far more questions of Pocognoli’s side. It feels like a task more suited to Hickey.

Scotland, collectively, will need to buck up their ideas if they are to stand any chance of emerging with a positive outcome or, at the least, some credit.

Scotland fans are desperate to see Gannon-Doak succeed but a little change might be needed.

There was a flatness to Friday’s performance, especially in a first half in which the much-vaunted high-press was conspicuous by its absence.

Sources indicate that the passing was too safe and predictable. The tempo was low and the play was unimaginative. By half-time, the visitors had fashioned the better chance when Enis Bardhi smashed the ball into the side net.

Scotland were markedly better after the turnaround. After Billy Gilmour’s scarcely believable miss, they were deserving of the opener which came when McGinn burst into the box and lashed home after fine work from Che Adams.

Stemming straight from a corner, North Macedonia’s equaliser – which ended their eight-game goal drought – asked a serious question of Pocognoli’s players.

To their credit, they stepped up with Gannon-Doak’s foray into the box causing the moment of indecision on which the game swung.

In a recent development, the manner of a first Hampden win for Pocognoli won’t live long in the memory. The fervent hope is that it proves to be the start of something.
