#26853. England's Euro 2028 mission starts NOW! Thomas Tuchel's men must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - or risk their 'DNA' cursing them yet again, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1314 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

England's Euro 2028 mission starts NOW! Thomas Tuchel's men must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - or risk their 'DNA' cursing them yet again, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1314 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:10 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • It is four months, almost to the day, since England shrank from the call of history and lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina in Atlanta but Thomas Tuchel may not believe that the Nations League tie against Spain in the Metropolitano on Sunday evening represents his best shot at redemption for the way things played out that afternoon in America’s South.
  • Industry observers note that that is largely because Tuchel does not appear to believe he has anything to redeem himself for.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:10 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 14 November 2026.

It is four months, almost to the day, since England shrank from the call of history and lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina in Atlanta but Thomas Tuchel may not believe that the Nations League tie against Spain in the Metropolitano on Sunday evening represents his best shot at redemption for the way things played out that afternoon in America’s South.

Industry observers note that that is largely because Tuchel does not appear to believe he has anything to redeem himself for. The manner of his side’s capitulation - and the substitutions he made - in the Mercedes-Benz Stadium last July enraged the nation, but Tuchel stated the fault was in the damned DNA of the English, that we were underlings, and that our players found it constitutionally impossible to keep hold of the ball.

Whatever Tuchel thinks, the fact remains that the tie against Lamine Yamal, Fabian Ruiz, Pedri and Mikel Oyarzabal and the rest of the world champions at the home of Atletico Madrid offers Tuchel and his players the opportunity to encourage themselves and their fans that they are not destined to be also-rans wired to fall at the final hurdle for evermore.

Spain are formidable opposition. They are on a record-breaking run of 43 matches unbeaten and have won their last 12 in succession. They haven't drawn a game since their June 15 game against Cape Verde in the World Cup. Their last defeat was on March 22, 2024, when they lost 1-0 to Colombia in a friendly. Some ask whether they are the best international side the world has ever seen.

‘Spain seem unbeatable,’ Tuchel remarked, when he walked into the press room at the Metropolitano on Saturday night and heard hymns of praise being lavished upon the opponents he is about to face.

In a recent development, ‘They have a very strong identity and a very strong mentality. We are trying to take it away from them. We are up for it. We are up for the fight. We are up for a spectacular match. We can see how far we can push the limits with the world champions in Madrid. The group is full of self-belief and rightly so.’.

England must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - even if they have flaws.

Thomas Tuchel must show he can find a way around the limitations presented by the 'DNA' he has complained about.

This may be the toughest game that Tuchel’s England side play until the European Championships in 2028, where the final will be contested at Wembley, and they will play all their games at home. They need to go into that tournament with the belief that they can beat the best when the pressure is at its highest.

Recent findings suggest that beating Spain away in the final game of the group phase of the Nations League is not quite the same as a critical match at a major tournament but it is as stiff a challenge as Tuchel is going to face until then. Beating Croatia 7-0 in front of gangs of schoolkids in Rijeka last month was hailed as the best England performance of the Tuchel era. Which says it all, really.

It was a great performance in a relatively meaningless match. Now it is time for him to show that he can marshal an England side to succeed against the very best, not fall apart when the prize is in sight. His protestations of powerlessness in the aftermath of the Argentina defeat were not a good look for a coach who was hired with the idea that his coaching prowess and his game management could get England over the line.

Has he learned anything from the manner of the Argentina defeat? ‘This game against Spain will be proof of concept at the highest level,’ he noted, ‘but we are up for it. I think we have taken the next step after the World Cup. The best thing is to trust our process and trust ourselves. We need to be clear about how we want to impose ourselves and I think that is all visible.’.

Now it is time for him to show that he can find a way past the limitations of England’s footballing DNA, find a way to compete with Spain and France when it really matters, and find a way to end the culture of near misses that has come to be England’s lot in the last decade of appearances in semi-finals and finals.

Sources indicate that england have played six matches since that day of crushing disappointment in Atlanta and scored 22 goals. But in the only one of those matches that really mattered, they lost 3-2 to Spain at Wembley in the opening tie of their Nations League campaign at the end of September, a game in which they were largely outclassed by Luis de la Fuente’s team.

Spain are what England have to aim for. Tuchel mentioned their example and their ability and their mindset straight after the semi-final loss to Argentina. ‘Ball possession plays a crucial role,’ he said at his post-match press conference in Atlanta. ‘It’s maybe not in our DNA like it is in our Spanish DNA or in our Argentinian-Brazilian DNA, to take the ball and control the game with the ball.’.

This may well be their toughest game until the final of the 2028 European Championships, if they get that far.

The England coach said more recently that England need to go back to trusting a traditional style that emphasises direct, high-intensity physicality rather than trying to copy Spanish patience in ball-retention. England, though, were taught a lesson in sophistication by the Spanish in September.

And for all the attention lavished on Yamal, Spain’s defence is the best in the world. Rodri, the shield for that defence and also the world’s best in the role, is not fit for this game but even without him, Spain’s back-line inspires an awful lot more confidence than England’s.

‘They were the best in the World Cup at the back,’ Declan Rice, England’s central midfielder, remarked on Saturday. ‘Defence wins you titles. Everyone talks about their attacking talent but you look at their central defenders, their full backs and the way their midfielders contribute to the defence, too.’.

That defence will have to stop England’s resurgent front line, led by Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane, who could be flanked by Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers and backed up by the supreme talent of Jude Bellingham just behind them.

Recent findings suggest that bellingham’s improving relationship with Tuchel, which cannot have been harmed by the inclusion of Bellingham’s brother, Jobe, in this squad, is another reason to hope that England still retain the capacity to improve after the World Cup. The elder Bellingham has become England’s most influential player.

In a recent development, england at their best would be one of the few teams capable of extending them. Rice said on Saturday that the game between the two sides was ‘massive’. England need to prove they can find a way to get closer to the world champions. To beat them, Rice said, would be a ‘massive statement’.

‘Playing against them is a great incentive to win. It will show where we are as a group. We are trying to attack teams full throttle and with players like Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers in our attack, it feels as if it is going to take off one night and maybe tomorrow night will be the night. We can beat Spain. For sure, we can.’.

Tuchel needs to prove England can win, not just be noble contenders. They need to prove that their DNA need not be a curse.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 01:04.

Manchester United have reportedly entered a three-way race alongside Tottenham Hotspur and Barcelona to land red-hot Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis.

Recently appointed Red Devils boss Mauricio Pochettino is desperate to reinforce his frontline during the January window, with the Old Trafford board poised to hand him a hefty transfer war chest.

Pavlidis has established himself among Europe's deadliest finishers this campaign, netting an astonishing 11 times across just 11 Liga Portugal outings.

The 27-year-old Greece star is believed to fancy a move to England's top flight and is seen as an instant improvement on the regularly sidelined Benjamin Sesko.

Now entering his prime, the ex-AZ Alkmaar attacker would bring immediate goals to Manchester without hampering the young Slovenian's future prospects once he regains match fitness.

Reports from CaughtOffside suggest Pavlidis features on a four-man shortlist of leading number nines currently under review by United prior to the mid-season market.

Pochettino is likewise rumoured to favour a link-up with Galatasaray talisman Victor Osimhen, a player the Argentine actively pursued while in charge at Chelsea.

Even so, a January raid for the Nigeria international looks improbable right now given his sky-high price tag and hefty salary expectations.

Ex-Brentford frontman Ivan Toney stays in the frame as a sensible stopgap option, thanks to his prior knowledge of Pochettino and eagerness for a Premier League comeback.

United scouts are also keeping tabs on Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy as a possible squad addition, although the 30-year-old is not viewed as a priority target at Old Trafford.

Apart from recruiting a proven finisher, United chiefs are ready to back Pochettino with fresh faces at the back come January.

Reinforcements at centre-half and left-back are widely anticipated as the Argentine manager attempts to halt his side's woeful league slide.

Much-admired Como stopper Jacobo Ramon stays firmly on the recruitment team's radar for the future, yet luring him out of Italy mid-season looks a tall order.

Elsewhere, Villarreal and USA defender Alex Freeman has been loosely touted for an Old Trafford transfer, though any pursuit is still in its infancy.

#26842. Red card for football chiefs as they announce ex-Premier League referee is dead aged 78 - when he is still alive and kicking

Red card for football chiefs as they announce ex-Premier League referee is dead aged 78 - when he is still alive and kicking

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (474 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:01 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 20:45 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • A former Premier League referee was mistakenly declared dead by football chiefs this week.
  • Sources indicate that on Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) announced Keith Cooper had died aged 78.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:01 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 20:45 EST, 14 November 2026.

A former Premier League referee was mistakenly declared dead by football chiefs this week.

Sources indicate that on Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) announced Keith Cooper had died aged 78. But he is alive and well.

The news reached the ears of the Wembley Cup final referee when he went out to his local sports centre for a flu jab only to be told: 'You were dead.'.

The Football Association of Wales posted a statement online and a tribute on social media to announce his death, but then withdrew it within an hour.

Mr Cooper, who is the father of former Nottingham Forest and Leicester boss Steve Cooper, told a Welsh sports website: 'I walked into the sports centre yesterday to have my jab and the fellow went, "You were dead!".

'Well, I'm not dead, I'm here and I'm OK!'.

The blunder appears to have emerged after the Wiltshire FA announced the death of another referee called Keith Cooper, who the football chiefs in Wales believed was the other Keith Cooper.

The FAW statement noted: 'Keith was a well-known figure who enjoyed an exceptional career at both domestic and international level and would later hold the position of FAW Referees' Officer following his retirement in 1996.

On Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) confirmed Keith Cooper had died aged 78.

Mark Beeney goalkeeper of Leeds United is Sent Off of by Referee Keith A Cooper for hand ball outside the area during the Premier League match between Manchester United and Leeds United at Old Trafford on April 17, 1996 in Manchester, England.

According to recent reports, former professional football John Fashanu is pictured with referee Keith Cooper during a Wimbledon F.C. match.

'Born and raised in Pontypridd, he is considered one of Wales' best match officials through his highly-regarded status in the game.

'In addition to his work with FAW, Keith was also a valued member of the Wiltshire FA Council who recognised his 'integrity, passion and commitment' in their tribute to his services to the game.

'Everyone at the FAW sends their condolences to his family and friends at this sad time.'.

Mr Cooper oversaw the 1994 League Cup final between Aston Villa and Manchester United, won by Villa 3-1, and worked in radio punditry after hanging up his whistle.

The FAW has not issued an explanation over the posted tribute. His family has not yet commented on the error.

But the unfortunate mistake has not spared the FAW from ridicule by other football fans.

One said: 'We always said there was only one Keith Cooper - turns out there are two.'.

Another remarked: 'Glad the whistle wasn't blown too early on Keith and much respect to the family of the other one.'.

Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, there is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn.

Sources indicate that at this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

In a recent development, dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

Sources indicate that the two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second indicated his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Recent findings suggest that max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

Recent findings suggest that “A joy to have him,” stated Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

Sources indicate that “Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z.

According to recent reports, dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” stated Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

Sources indicate that dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

According to recent reports, it was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” remarked Arteta.

According to recent reports, arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

Recent findings suggest that the only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Recent findings suggest that akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub.

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta stated: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”.

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:.

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady indicates Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf.

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”.

Recent findings suggest that he added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta mentioned: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”.

The record for the youngest hat-trick scorer across all professional tiers of English football belongs to Trevor Francis.

Playing for Birmingham City against Bolton Wanderers in Division Two on February 20, 1971, Francis scored four goals in a 4-0 win at just 16 years and 307 days old.

Max Dowman was first spotted by Arsenal at four years old. He’s been running past opponents and scoring goals ever since. Now he’s just doing it on the professional stage, in front of the watching world, but it still looks completely normal to him.

Chance! It could, and maybe should, have been four. Merino threads a wonderful through-ball beyond Ipswich’s final line of defence and Madueke steals in to poke the ball across the face of goal with the outside of his left boot. Gyokeres was in the middle but could not divert the ball goalwards.

Zubimendi gets us going again for the second 45 minutes. Konsa has replaced Gabriel at the interval.

Such is the midfielder’s versatility, his heat map tonight paints a wildly different picture to that from his 45 minutes at the Stadium of Light over the weekend. He has played the midfield-sentry role in Suffolk and has executed it well.

It is further evidence as to why Arteta was hell bent on signing him in the summer. You would imagine his all-conquering presence will relieve pressure from Rice and Zubimendi’s shoulders. They were out on their feet by the end of the last campaign.

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Industry observers note that their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

Sources indicate that it has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”.

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:.

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little challenges that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:.

“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”.

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:.

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies noted Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”.

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

Recent findings suggest that for much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

In a recent development, tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming.

Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom.

Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres.

Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz.

Max Dowman confirmed himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta mentioned: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”.

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

In a recent development, when asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil stated: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”.

Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

Industry observers note that the Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Gary O’Neil wins the rotation battle, raising Arteta’s nine changes with 10 of his own. Greaves the only survivor from last weekend’s win at Selhurst Park.

Your Town tonight! ✊ pic.twitter.com/EEYjPFww4Y.

Young defender Marli Salmon comes into the starting XI as Mikel Arteta makes nine changes to the team that started against Sunderland on Saturday.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Introducing your Carabao Cup Gunners starting XI ✨🤝 @deel.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

According to recent reports, after the match, the Arsenal manager stated: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”.

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

It has been revealed that this season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

Team news is expected imminently.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 01:39.

Appearing in the MLS Cup playoffs for the first time since 2023, the Latest England Revolution will welcome the Philadelphia Union to Gillette Stadium for game one of that best-of-three series on Saturday.

The Revs finished the regular season as the third seed in the Eastern Conference, losing 1-0 to Orlando City on Decision Day, while the Union wound up in sixth, defeating Toronto 4-1 in their final match before the playoffs.

It has been quite the first year for Marko Mitrovic in Upcoming England as the Serbian helped the club improve by 22 points from the 2025 regular season.

They earned twice as many victories in 2026 when compared to 2025, including seven more on home soil.

That said, they enter the post-season on a bit of a downward spiral, losing their last two league fixtures and scoring just one goal over that stretch.

At the same time, the club will try to end a four-match losing run in the post-season Saturday and win their first MLS Cup playoff encounter at Foxborough since the 2020 Play-in Round, when they beat Montreal 2-1.

Among all the 2026 Eastern Conference playoff teams, the Revolution were one the best defensively, conceding the second fewest goals (47).

On Saturday, they can extend their winning run versus Philly to three matches, having triumphed in both league games against them this year, including a come-from-behind 2-1 victory at Gillette Stadium in May.

Newly introduced England were not the only team with a great comeback story in 2026, as the Union transformed dramatically after an early-season slump.

Ryan Richter turned this team around, losing just two matches since taking charge in late May, after Philly had won just one of their first 15 league fixtures of the year.

Down the stretch of the campaign, however, the club regressed a little, dropping points in four of their last five regular season encounters.

This weekend they can snap a two-match winless run away from home versus MLS opposition, collecting six domestic victories in 2026, two fewer than the year before.

The Union have won two of their last three MLS playoff games as the visitors, including a 3-0 win at the Chicago Fire in 2025.

Philly have won three of their last four meetings with the Revs domestically and eliminated them from the 2023 post-season, winning that best-of-three first round series 2-0.

New England Revolution Major League Soccer form:.

Philadelphia Union Major League Soccer form:.

Both Peyton Miller and Leonardo Campana are questionable for New England in game one due to lower-body concerns, while Jack Harrison is doubtful with a quad strain.

Carles Gil was massive in the Revs turnaround campaign, leading the league in key passes (97) while Matt Turner became the third player in club history to play in every minute of a 34-game regular season.

At Philadelphia, goalkeeper Andre Blake left their last match with a groin injury, but could be ready to return, while Milan Illoski has a sore hamstring, Jesus Bueno is questionable because of a knee issue, as is Alejandro Bedoya with an eye injury and Japhet Sery Larsen is doubtful due to a concussion.

Cavan Sullivan netted a brace on Decision Day, with his brother Quinn also scoring and Bruno Damiani converting a penalty in the triumph.

Fresh England Revolution possible starting lineup:.

Turner; Feingold, Kohler, Fofana, Sands; Gil, Polster, Yueill; Fagundez, Turgeman, Gazdag.

Philadelphia Union possible starting lineup:.

Blake; Westfield, Pierre, Harriel, Wagner; C. Sullivan, Jean Jacques, Lukic, Vassilev; Damiani, Q. Sullivan.

The first match in the post-season is often nerve-racking for both teams, but we believe the experience and creativity of Gil will enable the Revs to unlock the Union defence and put them on top.

Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 43 min read (8631 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~43 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p-wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs.
  • Recent findings suggest that unconventional symmetry breaking in itinerant fermion systems has revealed some of the most remarkable phases of quantum matter.
  • Sources indicate that recently, spin group theory has provided a framework for identifying such magnetic states5, extending concepts developed for altermagnets12.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p-wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1,2,3). Achieving p-wave superconductivity4 and its magnetic analogue5—characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p-wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge6,7. Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p-wave magnets5,7,8,9,10, spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p-wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p-wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves Sy polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted Sy exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p-wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p-wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics10, topological matter7, superconductivity11 and beyond.

Recent findings suggest that unconventional symmetry breaking in itinerant fermion systems has revealed some of the most remarkable phases of quantum matter. A celebrated example is p-wave superfluidity in helium-3, where odd-parity Cooper pairing generates emergent orders beyond conventional paradigms1,2,3. Its magnetic analogue, the p-wave magnet, is characterized by an odd-parity spin-polarized electronic structure that preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation while breaking inversion symmetry5,6.

Sources indicate that recently, spin group theory has provided a framework for identifying such magnetic states5, extending concepts developed for altermagnets12. Whereas ferromagnets exhibit conventional s-wave-like spin splitting and altermagnets exhibit even-parity d-, g- or i-wave spin order12,13, p-wave magnets are characterized by odd-parity spin polarization associated with commensurate coplanar magnetic order that breaks inversion symmetry while preserving a combined time-reversal and translation symmetry5,14. The resulting electronic structure can exhibit a single symmetry-allowed spin component, symmetry-enforced nodal planes and a characteristic momentum-dependent spin texture. Candidate p-wave magnetism has recently been explored in insulating NiI2 (ref. 8) and metallic Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12 (ref. 9). However, spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for the characteristic odd-parity electronic spin texture remains limited8,9.

Here we present evidence for p-wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level (near-EF) electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi by combining symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations, neutron scattering and photoemission spectroscopy. Neutron diffraction reveals a commensurate spiral phase with propagation vector (0, 1/3, 0) below the upper magnetic transition temperature, TN1 ≈ 62 K, followed by a transition to a conical phase at the lower magnetic transition temperature, TN2 ≈ 33.4 K. Magnetotransport measurements indicate strong coupling between magnetism and itinerant electrons. Below TN1, spin-integrated angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, associated with strong 4f–5d exchange coupling. Spin-ARPES provides spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for the expected odd-parity Sy polarization in the near-EF spectral features: the extracted polarization changes sign across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p-wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Because the near-EF spin-resolved features contain contributions from multiple folded bands with momentum-dependent spectral weights, the observed Sy modulation is best interpreted as a spectroscopic signature of the expected p-wave spin texture at the level of the reconstructed electronic structure. Magnetic force microscopy (MFM) and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-µm chiral magnetic domains. Together, these observations identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p-wave magnetism in electronic band structures and related spin-symmetry-based phenomena.

In conventional ferromagnets and altermagnets (Fig. 1a), broken time-reversal symmetry permits even-parity spin-polarized electronic structures12. In the non-relativistic limit, conventional ferromagnets exhibit s-wave-like spin splitting, whereas altermagnets can exhibit d-, g- or i-wave-like spin-splitting patterns12,13,15,16,17,18. By contrast, unconventional odd-parity magnets can host p-, f- or h-wave spin polarization that preserves time-reversal (\(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}\))-related symmetry while breaking inversion (\(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{P}}\)) symmetry5. Commensurate chiral magnetic structures provide a natural route to such \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{P}}\)-symmetry breaking. In particular, coplanar non-collinear exchange fields can generate odd-parity spin polarization in momentum space when the magnetic structure preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}{\boldsymbol{\tau }}\) (ref. 5). As in conventional antiferromagnets, this symmetry enforces zero net magnetization in the ideal p-wave magnetic state (Fig. 1a).

According to recent reports, a, Schematic magnetic orders and their associated s-wave (ferromagnetic), d-wave (altermagnetic) and p-wave spin splitting in momentum space. Magenta and cyan spheres represent magnetic atoms with opposite spin orientations, related by the indicated combined spin–space symmetry operations in the d- and p-wave states, whereas blue spheres represent nonmagnetic atoms. b, Spiral magnetic structure of EuSi. The characteristic p-wave spin group symmetries are spin rotation combined with a glide mirror plane \([{C}_{2z}{||}{M}_{y}{\bf{t}}]\), and with a lattice translation \([{C}_{2}{||}{\bf{t}}]\), respectively. c, Calculated spin-polarized Fermi surface of the spiral phase, including SOC, showing p-wave spin polarization and spin splitting. d, Calculated spin textures near the top of the valence bands in the kz = 0 (bottom) and kx = 0 (top) planes, with (left) and without (right) SOC. e, Calculated spin-polarized band dispersion along the −Ym–Г–Ym (ky) direction in the spiral phase, with (left) and without (right) SOC. f, Conical magnetic structure of EuSi, with the combined spin-rotation and translation symmetry \([{C}_{6}{||}{{\bf{t}}}^{{\prime} }]\) indicated. g, Calculated spin-polarized band dispersions along the same momentum direction in the conical phase, with (left) and without (right) SOC.

In a recent development, we next consider the symmetry of the experimentally determined magnetic structures of EuSi. The crystal belongs to the point group D2h (space group Cmcm), and its magnetic states without (with) considering the effect of spin–orbit coupling (SOC) are described by the corresponding spin (magnetic) space group7. For the spiral state below TN1 ≈ 62 K, the spin space group is \({{}^{{2}_{y}}C}^{1}{m}^{{m}_{x}}{c}^{1}{m}^{{m}_{y}}1\), which satisfies the criteria for collinear p-wave spin polarization in momentum space. The spin space group breaks the \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{P}}\) symmetry, thereby allowing odd-parity spin polarization. The coplanarity of the magnetic moments, together with the spin-only symmetry \({C}_{2y}{\mathcal{T}}=[{M}_{y}|1]\,{=}^{{m}_{y}}1\), constrains the spin polarization to the y direction in momentum space. Combined with the \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}{\boldsymbol{\tau }}\) symmetry, the spin group symmetry prohibits the spin components Sx and Sz, while allowing a \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}\)-symmetric Sy component satisfying:.

It has been revealed that the spin-degenerate nodal plane at ky = 0, where ky is the component of the electron crystal momentum k = (kx, ky, kz) along the reciprocal-space direction corresponding to the crystallographic b axis, is protected by the combined spin rotation, lattice mirror and translation symmetry \([{C}_{2z}{||}{M}_{y}t]\), as illustrated in Fig. 1b. The corresponding spin-polarized electronic-structure calculations are shown in Fig. 1c–e. Figure 1d illustrates the calculated p-wave spin–momentum locking near the top of the valence band in the (kx, ky, 0) and (0, ky, kz) planes. The calculated bands obey the symmetry relations:.

Here, E(kx,ky,kz,Sy) denotes the electronic band energy at crystal momentum k for a state with spin polarization Sy along the b direction. Comparison of calculations with and without SOC (Fig. 1c–e) demonstrates that the characteristic p-wave spin polarization and splitting arise predominantly from the non-relativistic magnetic exchange, with only minor modifications from SOC. These calculations therefore provide the symmetry and electronic-structure framework for the p-wave state expected from the spin and magnetic (\({P}_{C}{2}_{1}{2}_{1}{2}_{1}\)) space groups of the experimentally determined spiral magnetic structure.

We next consider the conical state below TN2 ≈ 33.4 K. Its spin space group takes the ferromagnetic form \({{}^{{2}_{y}}C}^{1}{m}^{{m}_{x}}{c}^{1}{m}^{{6}_{y}}{t}^{{\prime} }\), characterized by a symmetry combining a six-fold spin rotation with translation, [\({C}_{6y}{|}{t}^{{\prime} }\)], as shown in Fig. 1f. Figure 1g reveals the calculated electronic structure without and with SOC. The calculated dispersions of the spiral and conical phases are similar over much of momentum space but differ near the Γ point (Fig. 1e,g). In the conical phase, broken \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}\) lifts the spin degeneracy at the Γ point that is protected in the spiral phase (see Supplementary Note 1 for further symmetry analysis). Accordingly, an anomalous Hall response is symmetry-allowed in the conical phase but prohibited in the spiral phase. The magnetic space groups of both phases are chiral.

EuSi crystallizes in space group Cmcm (No. 63; Supplementary Tables 1–3). Single crystals were grown by the Bridgman method. Scanning transmission electron microscopy indicates high crystalline quality with few crystalline defects (Supplementary Fig. 2), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis yielded an Eu:Si ratio of 50.2:49.8, consistent with stoichiometric EuSi within instrumental uncertainty (Supplementary Fig. 3). Two magnetic transitions occur at TN1 ≈ 62 K and TN2 ≈ 33.4 K, together with a weak structural distortion near the structural distortion temperature TS ≈ 60 K (Supplementary Fig. 4). Magnetization measurements along the three crystallographic axes show no pronounced hysteresis (Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 6), indicating the absence of net magnetic moments at zero field. Upon cooling, these phase transitions define two boundaries: from the paramagnetic to the spiral magnetic phase, and subsequently to the conical magnetic phase (discussed later). Upon applying a magnetic field along the crystal’s a, b and c axes (Fig. 1f), the conical magnetic/spiral magnetic state exhibits metamagnetic transitions associated with spin-flop processes, and eventually evolves into a spin-polarized state at high fields (Supplementary Fig. 6c,f,i). Angular-dependent susceptibility further shows a pronounced two-fold magnetic anisotropy (Supplementary Fig. 7).

Recent findings suggest that a, Temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility measured along the a, b and c axes under zero-field-cooled (ZFC) and field-cooled (FC) conditions, respectively. The magnetic transitions at TN1 = 62 K and TN2 = 33.4 K, and structural distortion at TS = 59.7 K, are labelled. b, Magnetization versus magnetic field along the three crystallographic axes at 2 K and 40 K. The inset magnifies the low-field region, showing no distinct hysteresis. c, Resistivity of crystal S1 with current along a. The residual resistivity ratio, RRR = ρxx(300 K)/ρxx(2 K), is approximately 262. d,e, Neutron-diffraction patterns in the (H, K, 1) plane at 40 K (d) and 6 K (e). f, Temperature evolution of the (0, 4, 0) and adjacent k1 satellite peaks between 5 K and 70 K. g,h, Refined spiral and conical magnetic structures at 40 K (g) and 6 K (h). The reference Eu moment in the a–c plane is aligned along a. This convention differs from Fig. 1 by a global rotation within the a–c plane, preserving the relative moment configuration and magnetic symmetry. i, Temperature-dependent intensities of representative k1 and k2 peaks, (0, 5/3, 1) and (0, 2, 1). The dashed lines mark the magnetic transitions. CM, conical magnetic; SM, spiral magnetic; PM, paramagnetic. f.u., formula unit; r.u.l., reciprocal lattice units; Q, scattering vector; j, electrical current density.

In a recent development, the longitudinal resistivity is metallic, with a residual resistivity ratio (RRR = ρxx(300 K)/ρxx(2 K) ≈ 262), where ρxx is the longitudinal electrical resistivity (Fig. 2c). A sharp resistivity change near TN1 and pronounced transport anisotropy accompany the magnetic transitions (Supplementary Fig. 8). Magnetotransport measurements further reveal a large, non-saturating magnetoresistance at low temperature (reaching 4,600% at 2 K with a 9 T magnetic field along b) (Supplementary Figs. 9–12). With increasing temperature towards the spiral magnetic state, the magnetoresistance becomes negative and remains so up to room temperature, indicating strong magnetic scattering in both the spiral magnetic and paramagnetic states.

It has been revealed that to determine the magnetic structures, we performed single-crystal neutron diffraction (Fig. 2 and Supplementary Note 5). At 40 K, satellite peaks appear at (H, K, L) ± (0, 1/3, 0) (Fig. 2d), corresponding to a magnetic propagation vector k1 = (0, 1/3, 0). Magnetic-structure refinement identifies an spiral magnetic order with moments rotating in the a–c (010) plane (Fig. 2g). The spins are approximately ferromagnetically aligned within each double layer and rotate by π/3 between adjacent double layers, corresponding to a threefold magnetic periodicity along b. This commensurate coplanar spiral is consistent with the symmetry requirements for the p-wave magnetic state discussed above.

Sources indicate that on cooling to 6 K, the k1 satellite peaks remain, while additional magnetic intensity develops at the structural Bragg positions, corresponding to a second magnetic propagation vector k2 = (0, 0, 0) (Fig. 2e). Refinement shows that this component corresponds to a ferromagnetic moment along b, yielding the conical magnetic structure shown in Fig. 2h. The persistence of the k1 intensity across TN2 supports the coexistence of the spiral and b-axis components within the conical magnetic phase rather than macroscopic phase separation. The refined ordered moments are mac = 4.4(1) μB per Eu at 40 K and mac = 5.4(1) μB per Eu, mb = 4.1(1) μB per Eu at 6 K, where μB is the Bohr magneton, consistent with the Eu2+ valence inferred from X-ray absorption and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism measurements (Supplementary Fig. 14).

The temperature dependence of representative magnetic peaks further resolves the two transitions (Fig. 2f,i). The k1 order develops below TN1, whereas the k2 component appears below TN2. Critical exponent fits yield β = 0.32(2) for k1 and β = 0.33(3) for k2, slightly below the classical three-dimensional Heisenberg value (β = 0.365), possibly reflecting additional spin–lattice coupling.

Industry observers note that before turning to the spin-resolved measurements relevant for p-wave magnetism, we first characterize the overall electronic structure of EuSi across the magnetic transitions (Fig. 3). The calculated three-dimensional Fermi surface in the spiral magnetic phase (Fig. 3b) contains several electron/hole pockets exhibiting strong anisotropy along the kx, ky and kz directions. Figure 3c shows the measured band structure in the kx–kz plane, corresponding to the cleaved a–c (010) plane in the conical magnetic phase. The constant-energy contours (Fig. 3c) show clear C2 symmetry and are broadly consistent with the calculated Fermi surface; similar dispersions are observed in the conical magnetic and spiral magnetic phases.

High-symmetry points are labelled. b, Calculated three-dimensional Fermi surface in the magnetic BZ in the spiral magnetic phase. c, Constant-energy contours at EF (i), EF − 0.1 eV (ii) and EF  − 0.2 eV (iii) in the kx–kz plane measured at 10 K. d,e, ARPES dispersion along the \(\overline{{\rm{Z}}}-\overline{\Gamma }-\overline{{\rm{X}}}\) direction, measured at 57 eV (ky ≈ 2π/b; d) and corresponding calculated bands (ky ≈ 2π/b; e). Here, b is the crystal lattice constant. f,g, ARPES dispersions measured with 7 eV photons (ky ≈ 2π/b; f) and corresponding DFT calculations at ky ≈ 2π/b (g) in the conical magnetic (i), spiral magnetic (ii) and paramagnetic (iii) phases. The α, β and γ bands are labelled. h, Temperature-dependent energy-distribution curves integrated near \(\overline{\Gamma }\) over the shaded region in f(i). Fitting resolves the peaks associated with α, β and γ. i, Temperature-dependent peak energies obtained from the energy-distribution curve fits. j, Corresponding energy separations between α and γ, β and γ, and α and β. Error bars in i represent energy uncertainties estimated from the energy resolution of the 7-eV laser-ARPES set-up at each temperature; those in j represent the corresponding propagated uncertainties in the energy separations.

The measured dispersion along the corresponding high-symmetry direction exhibits dispersive Eu 5d bands crossing EF (Fig. 3d). The measurement geometry, orbital-character analysis and determination of the high-symmetry points for the a–c cleavage plane are described in Supplementary Figs. 15 and 16. The bands near the \(\overline{\Gamma }\) point are labelled α, β and γ, and the band near the zone boundary is denoted φ, following comparison with the density functional theory (DFT) calculations in Fig. 3e. Differences in the number and precise positions of the calculated and measured bands may arise from the simplified treatment of magnetic structure, calculation parameters such as effective on-site Coulomb interaction U and lattice constant, and many-body effects (Supplementary Note 10).

In a recent development, over a wider energy range, ARPES reveals the Eu 4f- and Si 3p-derived states (Supplementary Fig. 17). The Eu 4f flat bands, labelled FB1–FB3, lie approximately 1–2 eV below EF and are further identified by resonant ARPES measurements (Supplementary Fig. 18). These states are crossed by dispersive Si 3p bands, consistent with orbital-projected calculations. Their location well below EF is consistent with the localized 4f 7 configuration and large local Eu2+ moment.

The magnetic transitions are accompanied by a pronounced reconstruction of the near-EF electronic structure. High-resolution laser-ARPES demonstrates that the α, β and γ bands evolve strongly across the conical magnetic, spiral magnetic and paramagnetic phases (Fig. 3f). Their characteristic energies shift by approximately 50 meV between the conical magnetic and spiral magnetic phases, followed by a more pronounced reconstruction at TN1, where the three bands merge upon entering the paramagnetic phase (Supplementary Fig. 19). Tracking their energy positions from energy-distribution curve fits (Fig. 3h–j) indicates that this reconstruction follows the temperature evolution of the in-plane magnetic order k1 determined by neutron diffraction (Fig. 2i). The calculations (Fig. 3g) reproduce the main evolution in the spiral magnetic and paramagnetic phases, whereas larger deviations occur in the conical magnetic phase, suggesting that the additional b-axis ferromagnetic component has a comparatively smaller influence on the near-EF electronic structure. Similar evolution of the α, β, γ and φ bands is observed at different photon energies and momentum directions (Supplementary Figs. 20 and 21), indicating a robust magnetism-driven reconstruction of the Eu 5d electronic structure.

We attribute this reconstruction to the strong 5d–4f exchange coupling between the localized Eu 4f moments and itinerant Eu 5d electrons through intra-atomic exchange19,20. This exchange lifts the spin degeneracy and accounts for the large band splitting with a gap of approximately 100 meV (ref. 21). Once the spiral magnetic/conical magnetic order develops, the enlarged magnetic unit cell also imposes a periodic exchange potential that folds the reconstructed 5d bands. This interpretation is consistent with the observed substantial Eu moment22. The Si p bands also show reconstruction across TN1, whereas the Eu 4f bands remain nearly unchanged in energy, although the intensity of FB1 starts to decrease at TN2 (Supplementary Fig. 22).

According to recent reports, the dominant effect of the a–c-plane magnetic moments is further reflected in the reconstructed electronic structure across multiple momentum planes, arising from the combined effects of exchange splitting and magnetic-zone folding. Consistent reconstruction is observed by ARPES on both the cleaved b–c (100) and a–b (001) surfaces (Supplementary Note 8).

We probe the predicted p-wave symmetry using spin-resolved ARPES on the a–c cleavage plane at 40 K. The relevant symmetry relations predict opposite Sy polarization under \({k}_{y}\to -{k}_{y}\), \(E(0,{k}_{y},{k}_{z},{S}_{y})\,=\) \(E(0,-{k}_{y},{k}_{z},-{S}_{y})\) and unchanged Sy under the corresponding \({k}_{x}\to -{k}_{x}\), \(E({k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z},{S}_{y})=E(-{k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z},{S}_{y})\) operation. By varying the photon energy, we sample a series of ky values across successive magnetic Brillouin zones (Fig. 4a,b; additional measurements from an independent facility are shown in Supplementary Fig. 34). At \(({k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z})\,=\) \((0,0.3\times 2{\rm{\pi }}/b,0)\) (cut 1 in Fig. 4d; b is the magnetic-supercell lattice constant), the spectral features associated with the δ, α and γ regions show negative, positive and negative Sy polarization of approximately 5%, respectively. At the corresponding negative-ky position (cut 4 in Fig. 4d; see Supplementary Note 9 for the band assignment), the extracted polarizations show the opposite signs. For intermediate ky values approaching the nodal plane ky ≈ 0, (also −0.5 × 2π/b) the net Sy polarization is strongly suppressed (cuts 2 and 3 in Fig. 4d), consistent with the node-like behaviour expected for an odd-parity spin texture.

These observations are consistent with the predicted spin symmetry but do not establish an eigenstate-resolved test because the measured features contain unresolved band contributions with momentum-dependent spectral weights.

To examine the momentum dependence more systematically, we extract the energy-integrated Sy polarization of the feature labelled α within the fitting-defined integration window at photon energies from 13 eV to 23 eV, sampling successive magnetic Brillouin zones. The extracted polarization exhibits a sign-changing modulation and is strongly suppressed near the ky = 0 nodal regions (Supplementary Fig. 33 and Supplementary Note 9). Despite the finite out-of-plane momentum resolution, the observed modulation is consistent with the odd-ky spin texture expected for p-wave magnetism and with the calculated spin-polarization patterns in both the lattice and magnetic Brillouin zones (Fig. 4b,c and Supplementary Figs. 35 and 36). The variation in modulation amplitude across successive zones is also consistent with momentum-dependent unfolded spectral weights, which redistribute contributions from folded magnetic-supercell states at different extended-zone momenta (Fig. 4b and Supplementary Fig. 36). The persistence of the same sign-reversal pattern in calculations with and without SOC (Fig. 4c) further indicates that the dominant spin texture originates from magnetic symmetry rather than SOC.

In addition, we find that the Sy polarization of the spectral features associated with the δ, α and γ regions remains unchanged within statistical uncertainty for symmetry-related points (kx, ky) and (−kx, ky), consistent with \(E({k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z},{S}_{y})=E(-{k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z},{S}_{y})\) (Fig. 4e).

Sources indicate that we note two limitations of the spin-ARPES analysis. First, the measured polarization is small, approximately 5%, compared with the calculated maximum contrast of about 25% (Fig. 4c), and the clearest spin-resolved features occur at finite binding energies within the near-EF electronic structure rather than at EF. The measured spin polarization may be reduced by finite energy and momentum resolution and by partial cancellation between unresolved contributions with opposite spin polarizations. Averaging over oppositely chiral magnetic domains could further reduce the signal if such domains are sampled within the illuminated area. Second, the near-EF features contain contributions from multiple folded bands with momentum-dependent spectral weights, and the cuts at positive and negative reduced ky were acquired using different photon energies and sample different extended-zone momenta, so the relative spectral weights contributing to a measured feature may differ. The measurements therefore do not constitute a one-to-one, eigenstate-resolved test of the calculated symmetry relations. In particular, the present data do not uniquely separate the momentum dependence of individual-band spin polarization from changes in the relative spectral weights of unresolved components. Within these limitations, the sign-changing Sy modulation and its suppression near the predicted nodal regions provide spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence consistent with the predicted odd-parity p-wave spin texture of the reconstructed near-EF electronic structure of EuSi.

The large local magnetic moment and its strong coupling with the electronic structure enable the measurement of the magnetic domains with different chiralities using complementary probes23,24. Figure 5a reveals the magnetic domains on the a–c plane measured by MFM in the conical magnetic phase, revealing a bubble-in-stripe pattern with a characteristic width of approximately 10 μm, corresponding to opposite spiral configurations. Similar stripe-like magnetic domains are observed by circularly polarized micro-ARPES with a submicrometre beam spot (Fig. 5b).

Sources indicate that figure 5c,d demonstrates the band dispersions along the \(\overline{\Gamma }-\overline{{\rm{Z}}}\) direction measured in domains A and B using right-handed and left-handed polarized light. Under circularly right-polarized illumination, FB1 and FB3 exhibit stronger spectral weight than FB2 in one domain and weaker spectral weight in the other, generating a clear domain contrast (Fig. 5c). Reversing the light polarization from circularly right-polarized to circularly left-polarized reverses this contrast, producing opposite circular-dichroism signals in domains A and B (Fig. 5e). The circular dichroism is associated with the orbital angular momentum of the Eu 4f bands with b-axis net moment25,26 (Fig. 5f and Supplementary Note 11). The calculated orbital angular momentum reverses between opposite magnetic chiralities, consistent with the observed reversal of the circular-dichroism signal. Thus, the micro-ARPES measurements reveal domains with opposite magnetic chirality and opposite b-axis moment.

Industry observers note that the temperature-dependent spatial maps in Fig. 5g show that the domain contrast persists in the conical magnetic phase, weakens in the spiral magnetic phase above TN2 and disappears in the paramagnetic phase. In contrast, MFM no longer resolves the domains in the spiral magnetic phase because of the absence of a net magnetic moment detectable by this probe. The remaining circular-dichroism contrast in the spiral magnetic phase may originate from domains with different chirality, although its microscopic origin requires further scrutiny. Overall, the domain-dependent circular-dichroism demonstrates the coupling between magnetic chirality and the electronic structure. Reversing the magnetic chirality therefore reverses the circular-dichroism response of the electronic states, providing a means to probe the chirality-dependent electronic structure associated with the p-wave magnetic state.

We now discuss the similarities and differences between p-wave magnetic spin splitting and the previously studied f-wave11 spin splitting in transition-metal dichalcogenides. Previous theoretical and experimental studies have demonstrated that in monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides (for example, MoS2), SOC induces odd-parity spin splitting in the valence bands27,28,29. Because this splitting is of relativistic origin in a non-magnetic crystal, it is relatively weak and cannot be easily tuned30. By contrast, first-principles calculations predict p-wave spin splitting in EuSi arising predominantly from non-relativistic exchange, whereas ARPES reveals a substantial magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure (Supplementary Table 6). Because this p-wave state originates from the chiral magnetic order, the calculated dependence of the spin texture on magnetic chirality suggests a possible route to controlling the associated spin polarization.

Industry observers note that compared with previously discussed ‘p-wave’ magnetic candidates8,9, EuSi provides a particularly clean realization of the archetypal p-wave symmetry setting8. In the spiral phase, the refined magnetic structure of stoichiometric EuSi preserves the combined \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}{\boldsymbol{\tau }}\) symmetry and has zero net magnetization, providing the symmetry setting for the predicted odd-parity p-wave spin texture without complications from finite magnetization. This combination has not been achieved in earlier candidate materials such as NiI2 or Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12. In NiI2, \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}{\boldsymbol{\tau }}\) symmetry is broken by the incommensurate non-collinear spin structure8, whereas in Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12 a weak magnetization breaks time-reversal symmetry and generates a large anomalous Hall effect9.

Recent findings suggest that furthermore, EuSi serves as an advantageous material platform because of its stoichiometric and metallic nature, and a relatively high temperature window (33.4–62 K) compared with those of low-ordering-temperature metallic counterparts such as CeNiAsO and Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12 (approximately 8 K; see Supplementary Table 7 for detailed comparison). Taken together, these attributes position EuSi as a particularly promising material platform for exploring and ultimately harnessing p-wave magnetism in electronic structures.

Recent findings suggest that metallic p-wave magnets are predicted to host unconventional responses, including field-free spin-polarized transport, a large non-relativistic Edelstein effect10 and non-relativistic Ising superconductivity11. When the spiral order is canted and forms a conical state, an unconventional and large anomalous Hall effect can be observed. Analogous effects, such as the magneto-optical Kerr effect, are expected to be pronounced as well. Through combined theoretical and experimental approaches, our results provide evidence for p-wave magnetism in the electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, associated with its chiral magnetic order and combined time-reversal and lattice-translation symmetry in the spiral phase (33.4–62 K). EuSi therefore provides a realistic and accessible platform for investigating symmetry-protected transport and optical responses driven by magnetism. Beyond fundamental interest, the controllability of its metallic and chiral magnetic states may enable field-free spintronic functionalities and pave the way towards engineering p-wave-correlated and topological electronic phases in itinerant systems.

EuSi single crystals were grown using the Bridgman method with an Eu:Si elemental ratio of 1:1. Eu (99.95% purity) and Si (99.99% purity) were mixed and placed in a tantalum crucible. The crucible was sealed in vacuum. The sealed tube was heated to 1,450 °C for over 12 h and maintained at that temperature for 24 h. The solution was then slowly cooled to room temperature. Owing to the sensitivity of the investigated phase to oxygen and moisture, the specimen used for the single-crystal diffraction experiment was prepared (mounted) in a protective atmosphere (an argon-filled glovebox). The single crystal used for this experiment was mechanically detached (cut) from the grown single crystal and mounted in a glass capillary (0.2 mm diameter) to prevent reaction with air and moisture during the data collection. Details regarding data collection and the refinement of the crystal structure are listed in the Supplementary Tables 1–3. Low-temperature X-ray powder diffraction was carried out at beamline ID22 of the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF). For this purpose, a portion of the grown single crystal was powdered, sieved through a 32-µm sieve and placed into a 0.3-mm glass capillary. The data were collected at specific temperatures using a helium-cooled cryostat and a multi-analyser stage for recording of the diffraction pattern. At temperatures below 45 K, the intensity of the beam was reduced using an attenuator to prevent the sample from heating up. The results of the low-temperature X-ray powder diffraction are shown in Supplementary Fig. 4.

Recent findings suggest that X-ray absorption spectroscopy and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism measurements were performed at the high-field magnet endstation of beamline I10 at Diamond Light Source, UK, with a base temperature of 5 K and magnetic field up to ±14 T along the direction of the incident beam. The crystals were cleaved in situ along the a–c (010) plane under ultrahigh vacuum, and the angle between the incident beam and the crystal (010) plane was kept at either 0° (normal incidence) or 70° (grazing incidence). X-ray absorption spectroscopy was carried out in total-electron-yield mode at the Eu M4,5 edges. X-ray magnetic circular-dichroism spectra were obtained by subtracting the absorption spectra measured with opposite helicities of the incident X-ray beam, which was aligned either parallel or antiparallel to the applied magnetic field.

Recent findings suggest that high-resolution ARPES measurements were performed at beamlines BL5-2 of the Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource (SSRL), A-branch of the Bloch beamline at MAX IV, and BL03U of the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility (SSRF). At BL5-2, a Scienta Omicron DFS30 analyser was used, achieving an overall energy and angular resolution of 20 meV and 0.2°. At Bloch and BL03U, a Scienta Omicron DA30L analyser was used, achieving an overall energy and angular resolution of 20 meV and 0.2°. High-resolution laser-based ARPES measurements were performed on home-built set-up (hν = 6.994 eV) at ShanghaiTech University. Data were collected using an electron analyser (DA30L Scienta Omicron). The total convolved energy and angle resolution were 5 meV and 0.1°, respectively. Micro-ARPES measurements were performed at BL07U of SSRF. The beam with photon energy from 88 eV to 102 eV was focused using a Fresnel zone plate and a spatial resolution of approximately 400 nm was achieved. The data were collected by a hemispherical Scienta Omicron DA30L electron analyser. The instrument energy and momentum resolution were approximately 15 meV and 0.01 Å−1, respectively. In all set-ups, the samples were cleaved in situ at approximately 10 K and measured under ultrahigh vacuum below 5 × 10−11 torr.

Industry observers note that the spin-resolved ARPES experiments were performed using a Scienta DA30L analyser integrated with a very-low-energy-diffraction spin detector at the National Synchrotron Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) BL13U. The samples were cleaved in situ at approximately 40 K and measured under ultrahigh vacuum below 2 × 10−10 torr. For these experiments, an effective Sherman function of 0.25 was used. Spin-resolved ARPES measurements at the U125-PGM beamline of BESSY II were performed using the spin-ARPES endstation equipped with a Scienta R4000 analyser coupled to two Mott-type spin detectors. The samples were also cleaved in situ at approximately 50 K and measured under ultrahigh vacuum below 2 × 10−10 torr. For these experiments, an effective Sherman function of 0.16 was adopted. The spin polarization was determined from \(\mathrm{Polarization}=(1/{S}_{\mathrm{eff}})\times ({I}_{\mathrm{up}}-{I}_{\mathrm{down}})/({I}_{\mathrm{up}}+{I}_{\mathrm{down}})\), in which Iup and Idown are the measured photoelectron intensities in the two spin channels and Seff is the effective Sherman function.

According to recent reports, the statistical uncertainties were estimated from the counting statistics of the two spin-detector channels. Assuming independent Poisson statistics, the measured counts Iup and Idown have standard deviations \({\sigma }_{{I}_{\mathrm{up}}}=\sqrt{{I}_{\mathrm{up}}}\) and \({\sigma }_{{I}_{\mathrm{down}}}=\sqrt{{I}_{\mathrm{down}}}\), respectively. Standard error propagation gives \({\sigma }_{{S}_{y}}=\frac{2}{{S}_{\mathrm{eff}}}\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{\mathrm{up}}{I}_{\mathrm{down}}}{{({I}_{\mathrm{up}}+{I}_{\mathrm{down}})}^{3}}}\). For energy-dependent polarization curves, this expression was applied separately to each energy bin; for the integrated polarization of a spectral feature, Iup and Idown represent the total counts accumulated within the corresponding energy-integration window. All shaded uncertainty envelopes and error bars in the spin-ARPES figures denote one standard deviation.

Sources indicate that neutron-diffraction experiments were conducted at the HB-3A DEMAND in the High-Flux Isotope Reactor at Oak Ridge National Lab. A piece of a EuSi single crystal with dimensions of approximately 4 × 3 × 0.1 mm3 was aligned in the (0KL) scattering plane and cooled. The wavelength used was 1.541 Å. The data were reduced using MANTID31 and ReTIA32. Symmetry analysis was performed using SARAh33, and magnetic-structure refinement was performed using FullProf34,35.

In a recent development, the first-principles calculations of the band structures and Fermi surface were performed by using the first-principles DFT methods implemented in the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP)36,37. The exchange-correlation and the ion-electron interactions are treated by the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof functional38 and the projector augmented-wave method39,40 under the generalized gradient approximation. Throughout all calculations, the convergence criteria for energy are less than 2 × 10−5 eV, and the plane-wave energy cut-off is set to 400 eV. The k-point sampling uses a Monkhorst–Pack scheme41 with an accuracy of 0.02π Å−1 for self-consistent electronic calculations. To correctly describe the strong correlation effects of the Eu f orbitals, the on-site Coulomb interaction was treated using an effective Hubbard U of 5 eV.

For electrical-transport measurements, a single crystal was cut into a bar shape. A standard six-probe method was used for longitudinal resistivity and transverse Hall measurements. Electrical-transport data were collected using a physical-property measurement system (PPMS; Quantum Design). Magnetic-susceptibility and specific-heat measurements were performed using a magnetic property measurement system (MPMS; Quantum Design) and PPMS. Thermal-expansion measurements were conducted in the PPMS using a homemade capacitive dilatometer.

Recent findings suggest that the MFM experiments were performed with a homemade helium-3 atomic force microscopy system using commercial piezoresistive cantilevers (spring constant k ≈ 3 N m−1 and resonant frequency approximately 43 kHz). The tips were coated with a nominally 100-nm-thick cobalt layer by magnetron sputtering. The MFM data were acquired by Nanonis SPM Controllers (SPECS) with a phase-locked loop. The MFM signal, the resonant frequency shift of the cantilever, is proportional to the out-of-plane stray field gradient generated by the sample. By using the constant-height mode, MFM images are acquired on a scanning plane approximately 200 nm above the surface.

E.C. and C.F. initiated the project. E.C., C.F. and Zhongkai Liu conceived of and designed the experiments. E.C. grew the single crystal, conducted magnetization and electrical-transport measurements, and analysed the data. M.Y. and E.C. conducted preliminary ARPES experiments, and observed large band splitting. Y.H. conducted the neutron-diffraction experiments and analysed the data. Zhongkai Liu proposed the possible existence of p-wave magnetism in EuSi, and Junwei Liu and Y.G. confirmed the chiral p-wave magnetism in theory based on symmetry analysis and DFT calculations. Y.Y., Jieyi Liu, H.C., Y.C., G.v.d.L. and Zhongkai Liu performed X-ray absorption spectroscopy, X-ray magnetic circular dichroism and ARPES experiments and analysis. Y.G., J.P., J.Z., J.A., Junwei Liu and L.Š. performed symmetry analysis and DFT calculations. Y.-T.C. and W.W. performed the MFM measurements. Z. Lu and H.W. performed the orbital angular momentum calculations. Y.P., U.B., V.H., R.K., W.S., P.B., M.H., D.L., X.S., L.N. and J.O. helped with data collection. B.H.G. performed scanning transmission electron microscopy measurements. R.L., A.F., J.S.-B., O.R., Zhanfeng Liu and S.C. assisted with spin-ARPES data collection. E.C., Y.H., L.Š., Junwei Liu, Zhongkai Liu and C.F. supervised this study. Zhongkai Liu, E.C., Junwei Liu and L.Š. wrote the paper with input from all authors.
